# 2020A Question 7 {.unnumbered}

::: {.exam-question}
## Question {.question-label}

[**Describe**]{.task-verb} the washout of desflurane from a patient following six hours of general anaesthesia. [**Draw**]{.task-verb} a graph to illustrate the description.
:::

Also asked in: [2014B Question 2](/content/exams/anzca/2014/B/2/index.qmd#examiner-comments)

:::: {#answer-structure}

## Suggested Structure

[**Describe**]{.task-verb} washout after six hours by linking compartment uptake to the subsequent concentration gradients and rates of elimination. Use the washout curve to connect the phases with their determinants.

::: {.structure-headings}
### Compartment Uptake and Saturation

### Washout Curve and Phases

### Tissues to Blood

### Blood to Alveoli

### Alveoli and Circuit
:::

::::

## Examiner Comments

::: {.examiner-comments}
The major domains assessed in this question were: A description of the shape of the washout curve. Factors which would affect the time course of washout. A graph illustrating the description.

The most common problem was that the graph did not illustrate the description. It is important to give some idea of the time course of the washout and to indicate in some way that the washout is some form of exponential decay. Marking important points on the graph make it easier to illustrate the description.

Other common issues were using the blood gas partition coefficient to explain tissue solubility or to say that low lipid solubility leads to a slow tissue washin but a fast washout.
:::
